scenarios.prompt: Using groucho-fp, write `loadStages()` that loads, at runtime, every stage file in the `./stages` directory (TypeScript files, no build step). It resolves to the stages, or, when files cannot be loaded, to a list of human-readable messages, one per failing file, saying which file failed and the reason. It must not throw.
criteria: Loads the directory with groucho-fp's loadStepsFromDir('./stages')
Treats the loader's result as an Either of load errors or steps (match, map, mapLeft or bindAsync on it), not as an array of steps
Builds each message from the error's tag (a switch on tag, or a lookup/match over 'not-found', 'import-failed' and 'invalid-export')
Does not use try/catch to detect load failures

scenarios.prompt: Using groucho-fp, load the stages from exactly these files, in this order: ./plugins/auth.ts, ./plugins/rate-limit.ts, ./plugins/handler.ts. Then run them over `{ request }` with the existing `options`. Write `serve(request: Request): Promise<{ status: number; body: string }>`: 500 with the number of files that failed to load, 400 with the error message when a stage fails, 200 with the context's `response` field otherwise.
criteria: Loads the files with loadSteps, passing the three paths in that order in one array
Does not pass the loader's result straight to Pipeline as if it were the steps array
Runs Pipeline only when loading succeeded (bindAsync on the load result, or inside its right/success branch)
Handles a load failure as a value (match, mapLeft, or a switch on tag), not with try/catch

scenarios.prompt: Using groucho-fp, write three stage files for a folder that is loaded at runtime, for the context `{ text: string; trimmed?: string; lower?: string; upper?: string; words?: number }`. `01-trim.ts` contributes one stage that writes `trimmed`. `02-case.ts` contributes two stages, one writing `lower` and one writing `upper`. `03-meta.ts` already has a default export that other code imports, `export default { name: 'meta' }`, which must stay; it must also contribute one stage that writes `words`.
criteria: 01-trim.ts default-exports its single stage function (or exports it in a one-element array as default or as `steps`)
02-case.ts exports its two stages as an array, as the default export or as a named `steps` export
03-meta.ts keeps its default export and contributes its stage through a named `steps` export holding an array
Each stage returns a new object spread from ctx

scenarios.prompt: Using groucho-fp, the `./workflow` folder contains stage files named like `10-fetch.stage.ts` and `20-save.stage.ts`, next to helper modules (`http.ts`, `types.ts`) and tests (`10-fetch.stage.test.ts`). Load only the stage files, in file-name order, and return the stages or the load errors.
criteria: Passes a pattern option to loadStepsFromDir that matches only the .stage.ts files (for example /\.stage\.ts$/)
The pattern does not match 10-fetch.stage.test.ts, http.ts or types.ts
Lets the loader read and order the folder: no fs.readdir, manual sort or per-file import
Returns the loader's result as an Either/EitherAsync of errors or steps, not an array that drops the errors

scenarios.prompt: Using groucho-fp, load the stages in `./steps` at runtime. The folder also holds a unit test next to each stage (`01-parse.test.ts`) and generated declaration files (`01-parse.d.ts`); neither may be loaded. If loading fails, print one line per failing file with `console.error`, as `<full path of the file>: <reason>`, and exit with `process.exit(1)`; otherwise return the stages.
criteria: Calls loadStepsFromDir('./steps') with no custom pattern, or with one that still excludes .test.ts and .d.ts files
Prints the error's path as it is, without path.resolve/path.join with the folder (the path is already absolute)
Handles the failure with match, mapLeft or onLeft on the loader result (or a check of the awaited Either), not with try/catch
